text:
maya.design: quick design review — chart legend + outlier-capping microcopy. attaching Figma mock. two quick UX problems: collapsed legend keyboard behavior is confusing; outlier capping truncates the y-axis but the tooltip copy doesn't explain why.

alex.pm: can you paste the mock here or a short gif? quick wins first: copy tweak + aria labels sound good.

maya.design: figma: https://www.figma.com/file/PLACEHOLDER/mock — mock shows small-multiples with a collapsed legend per row. proposal: legend collapse becomes a real button with chevron + sr-only text: 'Show series legend'.

leon.eng: for keyboard a11y use a proper <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls. also ensure a strong visible focus state. css snippet: ```css
button.legend-toggle:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); border-radius: 6px; }
```

sam.viz: about outliers — backend currently caps charts at the 95th percentile by default. we should surface that. options: show a small pill on the axis saying 'capped @95%' or mark the truncated points with an overflow marker. copy idea for tooltip: 'Values above the 95th percentile are summarized to improve chart scale. Click to view raw values.'

iris.acc: nit: avoid the word 'hidden' — implies deletion. suggest: 'summarized' or 'aggregated'. also add aria-describedby on the info icon and an offscreen explanation near the chart for screen reader users.

maya.design: alternative shorter microcopy: 'Top values summarized for scale — view full dataset in the table.' which is less technical.

alex.pm: product question — default cap percent and what happens on 'View raw'? open a modal or take the user to the table page? leaning to direct table view to keep modal complexity down. @leon.eng thoughts?

leon.eng: modal is doable but heavier. we already have the table at /metrics/{id}/table?range=...; I can wire the pill/tooltip to link there (open in new tab or same tab as product prefers). implementation detail: add `data-raw-url` attribute on the tooltip element with the table link.

sam.viz: one more UX bit — make the cap pill keyboard-focusable and include a focused tooltip pattern. also for touch targets ensure pill >= 44px.

maya.design: accessibility copy suggestion for the pill: aria-label='Axis capped at the 95th percentile; press Enter to view raw values'. we'll also add a screen-reader-only paragraph: 'Values at or above the 95th percentile are shown summarized in this chart to preserve overall scale; full values available in the table.'

chart-bot: New design note created: DGN-452 — Legend focus improvements + Outlier cap explainer. assigned to maya.design, due 2026-04-07.

alex.pm: copy candidate: 'Top values (≥95th percentile) are summarized to preserve chart scale. View full values.' anyone oppose? :eyes:

iris.acc: approve but small change: '≥95th' might confuse non-stat users. prefer 'the 95th percentile or above' for clarity.

maya.design: updated final copy: 'Values at or above the 95th percentile are summarized to preserve chart scale. View full values.' I'll update Figma components and export tokens.

sam.viz: extra note — legend collapse for touch: if collapse is per-row we must ensure tap targets are >=44px and chevrons have at least 12px hit area. check tokens.

alex.pm: :thumbsup: ok let's hand this to eng. @leon.eng can you pick this up for the sprint?

leon.eng: taking it. I'll create the story with ACs: 1) legend toggle is a11y button with aria-expanded/controls and visible focus, 2) cap pill shows tooltip + accessible aria-label + links to table, 3) touch target sizes verified. ETA: end of sprint.

maya.design: thanks — I'll attach updated components and the final microcopy in the ticket.
